newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sees Ecu future as possible EMU benchmark.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sees Ecu future as possible EMU benchmark.

text.p: LIFFE's three month Euromark future may be considered the benchmark euro interest rate future by financial markets but practical issues may shift this role to its Ecu future, a LIFFE official said on Wednesday.

"Although the Euromark is the benchmark we've also got the Ecu," Nick Carew-Hunt, market secretary at the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange told a conference on legal implications of a single European currency.

It will be easier to convert customers' positions in the Ecu interest rate future into euros on a one-for-one conversion rate than from Euromark futures into euros at a rate yet to be determined, he said.
The euro is scheduled to come into force in the final phase of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in January 1999.
He said LIFFE was considering a mechanism to merge its short term contracts into one single product, if and when appropriate, including a provision to convert Euromark positions into Ecu.

"We will set up a mechanism whereby people will be able to convert there positions from Euromarks into Ecu on a ratio basis," he said, adding there may be some sort of forced liquidation if only small bits and peices of Euromark trade was left over.
"If we do have some sort of forced liquidation...it's duty bound on us to provide some sort of mechanism at a low cost," he said.
